skill.name: global-validation
skill.description: Implement server-side validation with allowlists, specific error messages, type checking, and sanitization to prevent security vulnerabilities and ensure data integrity. Use this skill when creating or editing form request classes, when validating API inputs, when implementing validation rules in controllers or services, when writing client-side validation for user experience, when sanitizing user input to prevent injection attacks, when validating business rules, when implementing error message display, or when ensuring consistent validation across all application entry points.
skill.summary: Guides secure, consistent validation for application inputs across forms, APIs, uploads, and business rules.
skill.author: DevanB

security_audit.summary: Two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, not executable behavior or reconnaissance. The relative link in SKILL.md leaves the skill directory and depends on unscanned content, so it remains confirmed as a filesystem integrity risk. No prompt injection or additional semantic abuse evidence was found.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md links to a local path outside the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Include the referenced validation guidance inside the skill package or replace the parent-directory link with self-contained instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - When creating form request classes in `app/Http/Requests/` for validation logic
- When implementing business rule validation (e.g., sufficient balance, valid date ranges)

finding_verdicts.reason: The matched text is a Markdown inline code path, not Ruby backtick execution. It describes where validation request classes live and does not instruct shell execution.

Line 28 directs the agent to a relative path with ../../../ that leaves the skill directory and references unscanned local documentation. This creates a boundary and integrity risk because the skill behavior depends on files outside the audited package.
The text only gives examples of business validation rules. It does not request host, account, or environment reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Application inputs often drift across forms, APIs, jobs, and services. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical validation guidance for safer, clearer input handling.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of form request classes for validation logic in app/Http/Requests.
Applies allowlist validation for accepted types, formats, ranges, and required fields.
Covers API, form, controller, service, and background job validation entry points.
Encourages sanitization against SQL injection, XSS, and command injection.
Supports clear validation error messages for user-facing failures.
Addresses file upload rules, custom validators, and business rule validation.
limitations: Does not include the referenced validation standard inside the skill package.
Provides guidance only and does not run tests or enforce validation automatically.
Client-side validation guidance is limited to user experience; server-side validation remains required.
Framework-specific details may need adaptation outside Laravel-style projects.

use_cases.title: Build Laravel Request Validation
use_cases.description: Create form request rules with clear messages and allowlists for new web forms.

use_cases.title: Review API Input Handling
use_cases.description: Check controllers and endpoints for consistent type, format, and range validation.

use_cases.title: Define Validation Standards
use_cases.description: Align teams on validation patterns for forms, uploads, and business rules.

prompt_templates.title: Create Basic Form Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-validation skill to design server-side rules for a contact form with name, email, message, and clear error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-validation skill to review an API endpoint that accepts user profile updates. Identify missing type, format, and range checks.

prompt_templates.title: Add Upload Safeguards
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-validation skill to define validation for file uploads, including allowed formats, size limits, and user-facing errors.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Cross-Entry Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the global-validation skill to compare validation across web forms, API endpoints, services, and background jobs. Recommend consistent server-side rules.

output_examples.input: Ask for validation rules for a registration form.
output_examples.output: A concise rule plan covering required fields, allowed formats, password constraints, and specific error messages.

output_examples.input: Ask to review file upload validation.
output: Allowed formats and file size limits are called out.
Server-side checks are prioritized over browser-only checks.
Unsafe filenames and content handling are noted.

output_examples.input: Ask to align validation across an API and a background job.
output_examples.output: A consistency checklist for shared validation rules, business constraints, and error handling across both entry points.

best_practices: Define allowed input values, formats, sizes, and ranges before writing handlers.
Keep server-side validation as the source of truth for every entry point.
Return specific, actionable error messages without exposing sensitive details.
anti_patterns: Relying only on client-side validation for security decisions.
Accepting free-form input without allowlists or type checks.
Linking core guidance to files outside the packaged skill.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It guides secure validation for forms, APIs, services, jobs, uploads, and custom business rules.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is client-side validation enough?
faq.answer: No. Client-side validation can improve user experience, but server-side validation remains required for security.

faq.question: Can it help with Laravel form requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly references form request classes in app/Http/Requests for validation logic.

faq.question: Does it run validation tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance, but the user or agent must create and run the tests.

faq.question: What security issue was found?
faq.answer: The skill links to guidance outside the packaged directory, so the package is not fully self-contained.
